idea.title: Think, then act, then look.
idea.say: Here is the big idea of ReAct, in about a minute.

In 2022, language models were studied in two separate ways. Some only reasoned: they wrote out their steps, but used only what was in their heads, so they sometimes invented facts. Others only acted: they searched and clicked, but never stopped to think about what they found.
ReAct joins the two. The model writes a thought, takes an action, reads what comes back, and thinks again. Round and round, until it can answer.
Thinking makes the actions smarter. And acting keeps the thinking honest, because every new fact comes from the outside world.

idea.label: success on ALFWorld, from just one or two examples
idea.say: The result: on a household game called ALFWorld, ReAct beat the best other methods by thirty four points, after seeing only one or two examples.

method.title: One line of math.
method.say: How does ReAct actually work? It comes down to one small idea.

parts: normal actions: search, click, go to
method.say: Take the normal list of actions, like search or click. Then add one more kind of action: any sentence at all. That sentence is a thought.
An action changes the world, and the world answers. A thought changes nothing outside. It just gets added to the model's notes, so the next step is better informed.
And there is no training. The authors write a handful of example runs by hand, put them in the prompt, and a frozen model simply continues the pattern.

method.title: Thoughts can…
method.say: Those thoughts do many jobs. They break a goal into steps, pick out the key fact, add common sense, track progress, and fix the plan when something goes wrong.

demo.title: One question, two minds.
demo.say: Let's watch it work on a real question from the paper.

demo.title: Chain of thought
lines: Apple Remote was originally designed to interact with Apple TV.
Apple TV can be controlled by iPhone, iPad, and iPod Touch.
demo.say: The question asks what other device can control the program the Apple Remote was made for. Reasoning alone answers from memory. It guesses the Apple TV, and gets it wrong.

demo.title: ReAct
lines: I need to search Apple Remote and find the program it was designed for.
…originally designed to control the Front Row media center program…
I need to search Front Row next.
Could not find [Front Row]. Similar: Front Row (software)…
Not found. I need to search Front Row (software).
It is controlled by an Apple Remote or the keyboard function keys.
demo.say: ReAct thinks first, then searches. It learns the remote was built for a program called Front Row. Its next search fails, so it reads the hint and corrects itself. Then it finds the answer: the keyboard function keys. Correct.
That is the whole trick. Each thought aims the next action, and each observation corrects the next thought.

knowledge.title: A deliberately weak Wikipedia.
knowledge.say: Now the experiments on questions and fact checking.
The model gets only three simple tools on Wikipedia: search for a page, look up a word inside it, and finish with an answer.

knowledge.title: FEVER fact checking · accuracy
knowledge.say: On fact checking, ReAct beats chain of thought. And a hybrid, which switches between the two when unsure, does best of all.

knowledge.title: Why runs fail · share of failures
knowledge.say: The failures tell the real story. More than half of chain of thought failures come from made-up facts. ReAct almost never makes things up. It fails differently: by reasoning errors like going in loops, or by unhelpful searches.

knowledge.label: trajectories to fine-tune small models, and ReAct becomes the best method
knowledge.say: And with fine-tuning on just three thousand examples, even small models running ReAct become the best of all.

decisions.title: Long, messy worlds.
decisions.say: Next, two long and messy environments: a house, and a shop.

left.title: ALFWorld
items: A text game in a house

decisions.say: ALFWorld is a text game set in a house, with more than fifty steps per task. WebShop is a shopping site with more than a million real products.

decisions.title: ALFWorld · success rate
decisions.say: In the house, ReAct succeeds seventy one percent of the time. Acting alone gets forty five. And even ReAct's worst prompt beats every other method.

decisions.title: WebShop · success rate
decisions.say: In the shop, ReAct reaches forty percent, ten points above trained systems. Humans are still well ahead, at almost sixty.
And it's not just any inner voice. Thoughts that only describe the scene reach fifty three percent. Free reasoning reaches seventy one.

beyond.title: A mind you can edit.
beyond.say: Finally, what this means beyond the numbers.
Because thoughts are plain text, a person can read and fix them. In one run, a human deleted one wrong sentence, and the agent went on to finish the task.

items: Acting finds facts newer than the training data
You can see why it did what it did
Edit a thought, change the behaviour
beyond.say: Acting means the model can find facts that are newer than its training. And readable thoughts mean you can see, and steer, what it is doing.

beyond.title: Limits
items: Still behind trained systems on QA
beyond.say: There are limits. Prompts get long, it still trails fully trained systems on some tasks, and an agent that can act in the real world needs care.
But the loop it introduced, think, act, observe, is now behind most AI agents you use today.
